title: The 1936-39 Revolt in Palestine
author: Ghassan Kanafani
context: Written in 1972 by Marxist-Leninist author and PFLP leader Ghassan Kanafani, this foundational text applies historical materialism to dissect the great 1936-1939 Palestinian rebellion against British imperial rule and Zionist settler-colonial expansion. Kanafani analyzes the class contradictions between the militant rural peasantry, the emerging urban working class, and the compromising feudal-clerical Arab leadership.
relatesToToday: Provides an indispensable class analysis of the Palestinian liberation struggle, exposing how regional comprador regimes, imperialist powers, and settler-colonial institutions collaborate to suppress mass revolutionary movements, offering vital strategic lessons for contemporary anti-imperialist solidarity.
keyTakeaways: Identifies the tripartite alliance opposing Palestinian liberation: British imperialism, Zionist colonization, and reactionary Arab feudal and bourgeois leadership.
Details how the 1936 general strike and rural peasant armed resistance demonstrated the spontaneous revolutionary capacity of the popular masses.
Examines how feudal and bourgeois national committees repeatedly sabotaged militant mass mobilizations to broker compromises with British colonial authorities.
Demonstrates that national liberation from settler-colonialism cannot succeed under the political direction of compromising feudal and bourgeois elites.
Establishes scientific socialism and working-class leadership as necessary conditions for genuine anti-colonial emancipation.
